findings.reason: naming the enforced mode is what makes the discriminating arm of the gate reachable, and without it the node either stalls on an assertion that cannot pass or implements a second gate the deliverable does not want.
findings.text: s12's done-when asserts that the entry without `allow_unreviewed_plan` "is refused on the review gate", but the review gate refuses only in its enforced mode (`reckon/flight.py:1002`; absence is the report-only default, where the launch proceeds), and the gate names only "a temporary plan and crew home", so the one assertion that shows the waiver has its effect cannot hold as written — a node can satisfy it only by discovering the mode itself or by adding a batch-local refusal the deliverable does not ask for

findings.reason: one clause moves the dated record the deliverable asks for into the assertion and its control, so the gate measures the record the plan actually names.
findings.text: s14's deliverable requires the withdrawal to be kept "with its reason and date", but its done-when asserts only that the reason is kept and its negative control mutates only the reason, so a node that records a reason and no date passes the whole gate with a record the plan says must be dated

rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both units put their evidence in repository test files (`tests/test_a_batch_entry_carries_its_waivers.py`, `tests/test_a_decision_can_be_withdrawn.py`) and their base/head measurements under `all_debug`, naming no scratchpad or node-local path.

rubric_items.reasoning: pass — each unit's stated cause reproduces against the cited module (s12's missing batch field at `dispatch_batch.py:30`, s14's missing withdrawal verb and the overlap refusal at `_store.py:2005`), each endpoint is obtainable from the records named, and neither section prescribes a code path, step sequence or formula.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s12 delivers one capability (a batch entry carries the review waiver) and s14 delivers one op (withdraw a decision), with their refusal cases being validation of that one behaviour.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — neither changed unit adds a relationship it lacks: s12 depends on no other section's code (§3's ruling that the backlog waiver changes nothing is already true of the current tree, so the batch's refusal of `allow_unreconciled_runs` holds whichever order they land in), and s14 implements a tool capability whose "no longer holds any section" follows from removing the decision entry, so it needs no declared wait on §10.
